haiku-low.q1: The gateway returns 401 and does not touch any counter.
haiku-low.q2: All keys share one budget, so the total is the customer's plan limit per minute, 100 for Standard.
haiku-low.q3: A 429 with Retry-After, and the request is not forwarded. The backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. A rejected 429 request is not counted.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. It is counted, and the backend's 500 is returned with rate-limit headers.
haiku-low.q6: It is forwarded without a check, with no X-RateLimit headers, and ratelimit_store_unavailable is emitted. It may still be counted.
haiku-low.q7: Standard gets 100 requests per minute. Enterprise limit is TBD by Product.
haiku-low.q8: One Redis key per customer per window, rl:<customer_id>:<window>. Each key expires 60 seconds after creation, removing old counts.
haiku-low.q9: Windows are fixed clock minutes, so a new counter starts at each new minute.
haiku-low.q10: check_and_incr is a Lua script that Redis runs as one atomic step, so two instances cannot both take the last slot.
haiku-low.q11: Retry-After is 60 minus the current second within the minute.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED for retries. The client gets the normal backend response with no X-RateLimit headers.

sonnet.q1: Gateway returns 401; no counter is touched.
sonnet.q2: 100 requests per minute total if Standard (all keys of a customer share one budget). Enterprise limit is TBD.
sonnet.q3: A 429 with a Retry-After header. The backend never sees it (not forwarded).
sonnet.q4: No. A 429 request is not counted.
sonnet.q5: Yes. It was already counted, so a backend failure still uses budget.
sonnet.q6: Fail open: the request is forwarded to the backend without a check, and the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric is emitted.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: TBD (Product); not yet set.
sonnet.q8: In Redis, one key per customer per window named rl:<customer_id>:<window>. Keys expire on their own after 60 seconds (set when the counter is first created); no cleanup needed.
sonnet.q9: When the next fixed clock-minute window starts, a new counter key is used (the old one expires after 60 seconds).
sonnet.q10: The check_and_incr Lua script in Redis reads and increments the counter; Redis runs the whole script as one step, so two instances cannot both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: Seconds until the next minute starts: 60 minus the current second within the minute.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED whether it retries the store (the document says to forward without a check and keep nothing). The client gets no X-RateLimit headers; just the normal backend response.
